title: Assistance for Needy Students on School Meals Programme and for Home-Based Learning during COVID-19 Outbreak
what_it_is: Assistance for Needy Students on School Meals Programme and for Home-Based Learning during COVID-19 Outbreak

sections.label: Students on financial assistance meals
sections.summary: In 2019, about 49,000 Primary and Secondary students on the Financial Assistance Scheme benefited from the Schools Meals programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: In 2019, about 49,000 Primary and Secondary school students on Financial Assistance Scheme (FAS) benefited from Schools Meals programme.

sections.label: Household computer and Internet access
sections.summary: A 2018 IMDA survey found 98% of households with school-going children have a computer, and almost 100% have home Internet and broadband.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Based on a 2018 survey by IMDA, fortunately, 98% of our households with school-going children have access to a computer, and almost 100% have home Internet and broadband.

sections.label: Devices and dongles loaned out
sections.summary: As of last Friday, about 3,300 tablets and laptops and over 200 dongles were loaned to students without home Internet access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As of last Friday, we have loaned out about 3,300 devices, tablets as well as laptops; and over 200 dongles loaned out to students without Internet access at home.

sections.label: School spaces and NEU PC Plus
sections.summary: Schools can provide safe spaces for home-based learning with teacher supervision, and low-income families can apply for subsidised computers and free broadband via IMDA's NEU PC Plus programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: In addition, our schools can also provide students with safe spaces within the school premises so that they can come to school to use computers and the Internet in school, doing their home-based learning with supervision from the teachers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Those from low-income families can also apply for a subsidised computer and free broadband through IMDA’s NEU PC Plus programme.

sections.label: Meal subsidies and cash assistance
sections.summary: The member asks about the $50-plus monthly subsidy, noting students on financial assistance schemes get allowances via EZ-Link cards, and those at home are being helped with cash assistance from MSF and SSOs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This clarification may not be within his purview, but I wish to ask it anyway.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is $50-plus a month in subsidy, and of course, if they eat at home, then that is going to cost the family more expense.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: In fact, for financial assistance schemes today that the schools administer, we do give the students allowances and they typically use their EZ-Link cards to purchase meals in the canteens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Of course, now, some will still go to school and continue to purchase in the same way as it is today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But those who do not and are at home, that is what I mentioned earlier, we are working with MSF and the SSOs to provide additional financial cash assistance, given to the families so that they can continue to purchase the meals.
